2. The plaintiff opposite parties instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 518 of 1982 subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 183 of 1985 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for declaration of their title and recovery of khas possession of the property described in schedule 'A' to the plaint. The petitioner No. 1 being defendant No. 2 of the suit filing the written statement contested the suit. On 30.3.85 the petitioner No. 1 filing an application under Order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for amendment of the written statement on the ground that due to over-sight and lack of information, certain unintentional omissions and mistakes crept in the written statement. On 21.5.85 the application was allowed after hearing both the parties. Against that order plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 filed Civil Revision Case No. 584 of 1985 before this Court On. 19.8.87 the Rule was made absolute and the matter was referred back to the trial Court with a direction to dispose of the application after hearing both the parties afresh and giving cogent reasons for its decision. On 3.9.88 the matter was re-heard by the trial Court and the petition for amendment was rejected on the ground the proposed defence story was inconsistent with the earlier case made out in the written statement. Being aggrieved by the said decision the defendant petitioners have filed the revisional application and obtained the rule. 

 4. The subject matter of the suit is a portion of CS Plot No. 170 described by boundaries in the schedule to the plaint. The plaintiffs brought the suit for declaration of their title and recovery of khas possession of that property. In the written petition, Petitioner No. 1 has denied the material allegations made in the plaint. He also denied the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the disputed land. According to paragraph 26 of the written statement the suit land is a part and parcel of CS Plot Nos.171 and 172 and that the suit land originally belonged to Lal Mohan Chakraborty and that he sold the same to Abdul Hai and Abdul Latif in 1951 and that they in turn transferred the same to Abdus Sobhan, father of the petitioner No. 1 on 25.9.52. His further claim was that the building on the suit land was constructed by Lal Mohan Chakraborty and that Abdus Sobhan mutated his name on his purchase. By the proposed amendment the petitioner No. 1 wants to substitute the aforesaid paragraph No.26 by a new paragraph disclosing the manner of acquisition of the right of the suit land by his predecessor-in-interest. In the pro-posed amendment it is claimed that the disputed land is situated in Plot No. 170, and that Lalit Mohan, the predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendant, being the owner of the contiguous plots encroached upon a portion of CS Plot No. 170, constructed building on it and separated it by raising a pucca wall. It is further disclosed that Lalit Mohan Chakraborty adopted Lal Mohan Chakraborty who inherited the disputed property and subsequently sold the same.
